problem_framing.rationale: Frames the decision as posed: enter in 2027 or not, which route, against the $18M cap, 2030 payback, 8% margin floor and one-launch bandwidth. It uses these as criteria and names ad cost as the swing factor early. It treats the $40M ambition as a soft 'direction' to confirm with the board rather than as a trade-off against the constraints. 'No US entry' is only named and not developed.

storyline_coherence.rationale: Clear governing thought, with the summary mapped to sections: Amazon meets limits, retail breaks them, ACoS is the swing factor, then gates. Most titles are claims. Weaknesses: four divider slides all titled 'The US is worth entering', and the contents slide headings are mislabelled. The exec summary says Amazon 'meets' payback while the body shows it is marginal. The 'Japan becomes better above 28.6%' trigger sits awkwardly with slide 31, where Japan already returns more cash at 28%. The slide 6 claim that 'most new spend is going to Korean brands' contradicts its own 38.6% figure.

evidence_and_reasoning.rationale: Core numbers check out: A $4.73 per unit at 25% ACoS, cumulative cash +2.40/+0.38/−2.32, break-even ACoS 28.6%, tariff cost ~$1.1M, B −$20.8M and 4.5% margin, break-even of 19.1 units per door, Option J. The 32% benchmark and the 2.6 median against the 4.0 cut-off are used, and the correlation is challenged correctly. Weaknesses: the pre-ad $10.72 contribution and the $4.00 at 28% are not stated explicitly. Slide 6 misreads 'most new spend' when K-beauty is 38.6% of growth. 'US buyers rate it as Korean buyers do' has no source. The 2032 extrapolation and the assumed awareness base are shaky. CAGR is not given, but the growth totals are.

strategic_judgment.rationale: Amazon-led entry with five quarterly gates (ACoS 28.6%, repeat 31%, revenue, peak cash, awareness 20%), a Japan fallback and a stall-case downside of $7M. This matches the defensible route and avoids all the traps. It names what would change the answer and gives owners and next steps. Option B is rejected on cap and margin grounds, and the retail trigger is raised from 15% to 20%. Gaps: it does not clearly say the $40M ambition is unreachable within the constraints, since it reads it as 'two years late' with an extrapolated 29% growth. It also gives Japan only a fallback role even though Japan returns more cash at pilot ACoS.

clarity_and_concision.rationale: The answer is on slide 3 and most slides are crisp. But 45 slides, four duplicate dividers with wrong titles, repeated retail-rebuttal slides (18–23) and several backups are more than the decision needs. Some jargon and cross-reference tags such as (4b) remain.

unsupported_claims.quote: Product quality travels: US buyers rate it as Korean buyers do
unsupported_claims.why: The pack gives no Korean rating, so the comparison is invented.

unsupported_claims.quote: Other brands: grew slowly, so most new spend is going to Korean brands
unsupported_claims.why: K-beauty added $1.7B of the $4.4B category growth (38.6%), which the slide itself reports. Other brands added more.

unsupported_claims.quote: For a newcomer: a growing segment lets Onsoo win buyers without taking them from incumbents
unsupported_claims.why: This is an assertion with no evidence in the pack.

unsupported_claims.quote: Every month up: growth never paused, a sign of word of mouth and reviews, not a one-off promotion
unsupported_claims.why: This is a causal reading of six months of data on a small base. It is not established by the pack.

unsupported_claims.quote: Aided awareness of 4% is among all survey respondents, who are all facial skincare buyers, the base Table 8 uses
unsupported_claims.why: The pack does not say what base Table 8 uses.
The 29% growth is extrapolated as if it were sustained, which flatters the 'gap is only timing' reading and rests on the planning ACoS.

logical_contradictions.quote_a: Other brands: grew slowly, so most new spend is going to Korean brands
logical_contradictions.quote_b: K-beauty share of the category's growth 38.6%
logical_contradictions.why: If K-beauty captured only 38.6% of growth, most new spend is not going to Korean brands.

logical_contradictions.quote_a: Ad cost is the swing factor: payback needs ACoS at or below 28.6%; above that, Japan becomes the better 2027 choice
logical_contradictions.quote_b: Japan returns more cash by 2030 unless ad cost holds at plan (Amazon-led 28% ends 2030 at $0.38M vs Japan $1.8M)
logical_contradictions.why: Japan already beats the US on 2030 cash at 28% ACoS, below the 28.6% switch threshold, so the gate and the comparison do not line up.

recommendation.summary: Launch Amazon-led in 2027 with five quarterly gates (ACoS ≤28.6%, repeat ≥31%, revenue, peak cash, awareness >20% before any retail test). Add retail only as a targeted door test. Keep Japan as the fallback if ACoS stays above break-even. Reject national retail.
recommendation.rationale: It matches R1: Amazon entry with explicit gates, the ACoS break-even, the label fix, a tariff re-run, retail only when awareness supports it, and rejection of Option B. It meets the defensibility criteria, since it compares options on the board's constraints, tests the ACoS and units-per-door assumptions, and states what has to be true. It is weaker on explicitly resetting the $40M ambition.

hypothesis_handling.rationale: The CEO's Amazon-first plan is kept with three changes: the retail trigger moves to awareness above 20%, ACoS is gated at the 28.6% break-even rather than assumed to fall to 25%, and retail becomes a targeted test. This is the expected handling. The deck tests the 25% ACoS against the 32% benchmark and the 4.5 units per door against the 2.6 median. It does not fully reset the $40M ambition and calls the gap 'timing'.

output.overall_comment: This is a strong, numerically accurate deck. The Amazon-with-gates recommendation is defensible and every key calculation (A at 25/28/32% ACoS, B at −$20.8M and 4.5% margin, the 28.6% break-even, the tariff) matches the answer key. It uses the awareness-versus-sell-through evidence well and rebuts the correlation memo and the $5.2B figure. Flaws: a misread on slide 6 ('most new spend'), a few unsupported assertions, a soft treatment of the $40M ambition, a slight mismatch between the Japan switch threshold and the cash comparison, and 45 slides with duplicated divider slides.
